question: Points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D\) have these coordinates: \(A(3,2),\) \(B(3,-2),\) \(C(-3,-2)\) and \(D(-3,0).\) What is the area of quadrilateral \(ABCD?\)
solution:
Complete the quadrilateral to a rectangle by adding the point \(E=(-3,2)\). The coordinates show that \(ABCE\) is a rectangle of width \(3-(-3)=6\) and height \(2-(-2)=4\).

The point \(D=(-3,0)\) lies on side \(CE\). Thus the part of the rectangle outside \(ABCD\) is right triangle \(AED\), whose perpendicular legs have lengths \(AE=6\) and \(ED=2-0=2\). Subtracting its area gives
\[
\text{Area}(ABCD)=6\times4-\frac{6\times2}{2}=24-6=18.
\]
The area is \(18\) square units, choice C.

solutionMethods.explanation:
Points \(A\) and \(B\) both have horizontal coordinate \(3\), so \(AB\) is vertical and has length \(2-(-2)=4\). Points \(C\) and \(D\) both have horizontal coordinate \(-3\), so \(CD\) is vertical and has length \(0-(-2)=2\).

These opposite sides are parallel, making \(ABCD\) a trapezoid. Their perpendicular separation is the horizontal distance \(3-(-3)=6\). Using the parallel sides as the bases, its area is
\[
\frac{4+2}{2}\times6=18.
\]
The area is \(18\) square units, choice C.
solutionMethods.label: Use the trapezoid formula
